args.sql: select count(*), count(distinct payment_id), count(distinct payment_id||'-'||cdc_seq), sum(amount), max(amount), sum(case when cdc_op='U' then 1 else 0 end) from raw.payments where payment_date >= '2026-10-01' group by all

select _ds, count(*) n, count(distinct payment_id) dp, count(distinct (payment_id, cdc_seq)) dps, sum(case when cdc_op='U' then 1 else 0 end) u, max(amount), min(payment_date), max(payment_date) from raw.payments where _ds >= '2026-09-21' group by 1 order by 1
select ds, count(*), count(distinct payment_id), sum(amount) from main.stg_payments where ds >= '2026-10-01' group by 1 order by 1

select count(*) from (select payment_id, cdc_seq, count(distinct (loan_id, amount, principal_amount, interest_amount, cdc_op, payment_date)) c from raw.payments where _ds='2026-10-06' group by 1,2 having c>1)

args.summary: Contract breach on keel_payments v2.1 (cc vendor-management@harborlending.example). File landing/payments/keel_payments_20261007.csv (arrived 2026-10-08 03:53) renames required column 'loan_id' to 'loan_number' (header: payment_id,loan_number,payment_date,amount,principal_amount,interest_amount,cdc_op,cdc_seq). This is a breaking column rename sent without the 30-day notice the contract requires. Harbor's ingest_payments rejected the file (SchemaMismatchError, 3 attempts), so business day 2026-10-07 payments are not loaded and the delinquency mart for 2026-10-07 is not published. Action needed: please re-send the 2026-10-07 file with the contract v2.1 header (loan_id) as keel_payments_20261007_r1.csv as soon as possible. If you plan to rename the column, announce it with 30 days' notice. Separately, FYI: the 2026-10-06 file contained 119 replayed CDC events (357 rows, 238 unique payment_id/cdc_seq), which looks like a connector restart. Our staging deduplicates these, so you don't need to do anything about it.

The 2026-10-06 raw.payments spike comes from 119 identical replayed CDC events (357 rows, 238 distinct payment_id/cdc_seq, no conflicting values, and the trailer count of 357 matches). stg_payments deduplicates them to 230 payments, in line with other days, so the marts are not affected.

args.evidence: ["ALR-66710B", "ALR-9A50BE", "ALR-A3B808", "ALR-1E9D25", "ALR-B5F08F", "landing/payments/keel_payments_20261007.csv header: loan_number instead of loan_id", "tr-000168/tr-000169/tr-000170 SchemaMismatchError", "contract keel_payments v2.1 change_policy: 30 days' notice; no announcement or contract change", "raw.payments _ds=2026-10-06: 357 rows, 238 distinct (payment_id,cdc_seq), identical replays; stg_payments 230 rows"]}
args.summary: Keel Servicing renamed the required column loan_id to loan_number in its 2026-10-07 payments file without the 30-day notice the contract requires. ingest_payments rejected the file, as it should, so raw.payments and mart_delinquency are stale for 2026-10-07. Nothing bad was loaded, so I quarantined nothing. Following the contract and the schema runbook, I left the pipeline unchanged and escalated to Keel, asking them to re-send the file with the contract header as _r1. Once it arrives, re-run ingest_payments for 2026-10-07. The 2026-10-06 volume alert was caused by identical replayed CDC events that stg_payments deduplicates, so I closed it as expected.
